name: St. Rita
bio:
Rita of Cascia was born in 1381 near Cascia, Italy. Married at a young age to a violent man, she endured his abuse with patience and prayer, and eventually won his conversion. After her husband was murdered in a feud and her two sons died, Rita sought to enter the Augustinian convent at Cascia, where she was at first refused.

She was finally admitted around 1413 and lived there for forty years in prayer, penance, and service. In her later years she received a wound on her forehead, understood as a share in Christ's crown of thorns, which she bore until her death in 1457.

She is known as the saint of the impossible, invoked in hopeless marriages, family conflicts, and causes that seem beyond human help. She was canonized in 1900.
